--- title: "[GammaLS]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Gamma location-scale family for GAMLSS. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L16-L304){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python GammaLS() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `GammaLS` extends the plain `Gamma` family by letting both the mean `mu` and the coefficient of variation `sigma` vary smoothly with covariates, instead of assuming a fixed shape parameter. Use it for strictly positive, right-skewed responses where not only the typical magnitude but also the relative spread (coefficient of variation) changes systematically across the range of the predictors — for example, cost or duration data whose relative volatility grows with the covariates rather than staying proportional to `mu` alone. Both parameters use the log link, keeping `mu > 0` and `sigma > 0`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} `GammaLS` parameterizes the Gamma distribution by its mean `mu > 0` and its coefficient of variation `sigma > 0`, where `sigma = 1 / sqrt(shape)` and `shape = alpha = 1 / sigma^2`. Both parameters use the log link: $$ g_{\mu}(\mu) = \log(\mu), \qquad g_{\sigma}(\sigma) = \log(\sigma). $$ The response density is the Gamma density with shape `alpha = 1/sigma^2` and rate `alpha/mu`: $$ f(y \mid \mu, \sigma) = \frac{(\alpha/\mu)^{\alpha}}{\Gamma(\alpha)}\, y^{\alpha - 1} \exp\!\left(-\frac{\alpha y}{\mu}\right), \qquad \alpha = \frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}. $$ Because `sigma` is the coefficient of variation, $\operatorname{Var}(Y) = \sigma^2 \mu^2$, so this is a direct generalization of `Gamma`'s variance function `V(mu) = mu^2` in which the proportionality constant `sigma^2` is itself allowed to depend on covariates. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAMLSS where both the mean and relative spread of a positive response vary smoothly: ::: {#800f9330 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = np.exp(1.0 + 0.4 * np.sin(x)) sigma = 0.2 + 0.15 * np.abs(np.cos(x)) shape = 1.0 / sigma**2 y = rng.gamma(shape, mu / shape) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAMLSS( formulas={"mu": "y ~ s(x)", "sigma": "y ~ s(x)"}, family=wk.GammaLS(), ) model.fit(data) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAMLSS fit summary ======================================== Family: GammaLS(mu=log, sigma=log) N obs: 300 Global deviance: 666.8366 AIC: 690.3882 BIC: 734.0031 Log-likelihood: -333.4183 Converged: True (5 iterations) --- mu --- EDF total: 5.93 Smooth 1: edf = 4.93 --- sigma --- EDF total: 5.84 Smooth 1: edf = 4.84 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
parameter_names Names of the distributional parameters modeled by `GammaLS`.
### [parameter_names]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Names of the distributional parameters modeled by `GammaLS`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [parameter_names]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description

dl_dtheta() First derivative of the Gamma log-likelihood with respect to `mu` or `sigma`.

link() Apply the log link for `mu` or `sigma`.

### [d2l_dtheta2()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Expected Fisher information for `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L189-L223){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python d2l_dtheta2(param, y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} With shape `alpha = 1/sigma^2` and trigamma function $\psi_1$: $$ -E\!\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = \frac{\alpha}{\mu^2}, \qquad -E\!\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2}\right] = \frac{4}{\sigma^4}\big(\alpha\,\psi_1(\alpha) - 1\big). $$ The `sigma` term is additionally floored at `_SIGMA_FLOOR` to keep the working weight strictly positive. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)` (unused, kept for interface consistency). [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"sigma"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise working weights, shape `(n,)`, guaranteed positive. ::: ### [dl_dtheta()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} First derivative of the Gamma log-likelihood with respect to `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L152-L187){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python dl_dtheta(param, y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} With shape `alpha = 1/sigma^2`, the score functions are $$ \frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \frac{\alpha}{\mu}\left(\frac{y}{\mu} - 1\right), \qquad \frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \sigma} = \frac{2}{\sigma^3}\left( \psi(\alpha) - \log\alpha - \log\frac{y}{\mu} - 1 + \frac{y}{\mu}\right), $$ where $\psi$ is the digamma function. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"sigma"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise first derivatives, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Starting values for `mu` and `sigma` from the raw response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L256-L277){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `mu` is initialized at the (floored) observed values themselves, and `sigma` at the sample coefficient of variation of `y` (clamped to at least `0.1`), constant across observations. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `{"mu": y_safe.copy(), "sigma": }`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the log link for `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L88-L106){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(param, values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Both parameters use the log link, so `values` are first floored (`_MU_FLOOR` for `mu`, `_SIGMA_FLOOR` for `sigma`) to avoid `log(0)` before taking the logarithm. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `log(values)`, with `values` clamped away from zero first. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the log link for `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L130-L150){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(param, values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For the log link, $d\eta/d\theta = 1/\theta$ for either parameter. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"`, used only to select the appropriate numerical floor. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale at which to evaluate the derivative, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `1 / values`, with `values` clamped away from zero first. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the inverse log link for `mu` or `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L108-L128){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(param, eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `eta` is clipped to `[-_ETA_MAX, _ETA_MAX]` before exponentiating, guarding against overflow when the additive predictor drifts to extreme values during fitting. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either `"mu"` or `"sigma"` (unused directly, since both share the log link). [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Additive predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `exp(eta)` after clipping `eta` for numerical stability. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total Gamma log-likelihood at the current `mu` and `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L225-L254){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Evaluated using the shape/rate parameterization `alpha = 1/sigma^2`, `rate = alpha/mu`, with `y` and `mu` floored at `_MU_FLOOR` and `sigma` floored at `_SIGMA_FLOOR` for numerical stability. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"sigma"`, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The log-likelihood summed over all observations. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate response values from a Gamma distribution with the given `mu`, `sigma`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gamma_ls.py#L279-L301){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(params, rng) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Converts to the shape/scale parameterization (`shape = 1/sigma^2`, `scale = mu * sigma^2`) expected by `rng.gamma`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates with keys `"mu"` and `"sigma"`, each of shape `(n,)`. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [np.random.Generator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A NumPy random generator used to draw the simulated values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values, shape `(n,)`. :::
